rubric.role_summary: Founding machine learning engineer building production ML and LLM systems for autonomous commercial insurance underwriting, owning the lifecycle from data through deployment and evaluation.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Founding machine learning engineer building production ML and LLM systems for autonomous commercial insurance underwriting, owning the lifecycle from data through deployment and evaluation.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- 4+ years of industry experience building and deploying ML systems to production.
- Experience fine-tuning SLMs or LLMs.
- Deep proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks; the named frameworks are examples, not a requirement to know all of them.
- Production LLM application experience.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Experience using fine-tuning techniques such as RLHF, DPO, or LoRA.
- Familiarity with document parsing, information extraction, or NLP on unstructured business documents.
- Background in insurance, finance, or other high-stakes structured domains where model errors have real consequences.
- Experience with agentic frameworks or multi-step LLM orchestration.
- Confidence calibration experience.
- TypeScript proficiency.
- Familiarity with data pipelines using SQL, dbt, Spark, or equivalent.
- MS or PhD in a quantitative field such as ML/AI, statistics, math, or physics.
- 4+ years of industry experience building and shipping ML systems end-to-end, from raw data to production models, including experience with model deployment platforms; AWS SageMaker is an example, not a required platform.
- Production LLM experience encompassing prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool use, evaluation, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Experience building reliable models with limited labeled data, including synthetic data generation, data augmentation, or similar techniques.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): San Francisco Bay Area, California. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them. Onsite work is based in one of these areas.
